messages:
tara: quick heads-up — a customer reported their SIEM parser is failing on our S3 audit export. they see 400s from Splunk because timestamps and event_type are nested differently than their mapping. can we triage schema + delivery details?
kevin-w: on it. do we know which delivery method? webhook or s3?
tara: S3 export first, webhook might be affected by the same schema change. customer mentioned SSE-KMS encryption too — their ingestion lambda couldn't decrypt after our recent key rotation.
olivia: hmm — two separate issues then: 1) schema shape, 2) KMS key access for their role. for schema: did we recently add event.actor_display or changed actor.email -> actor_email?
kevin-w: we added a flat "actor_display" as part of the RBAC audit work last week, and normalized user identifiers to always include "actor_id" and "actor_email" when available. that change was gated behind the feature flag but got rolled to a subset of tenants. maybe customer got mixed-format files.
sec-bot: deploy-bot: deployment abc123 completed to prod at 1758456700 :white_check_mark: 
support-sam: customer is onboarding org: acme-telemetry. they need a reproducible payload example they can feed into their parsers and also a signed webhook test for their SIEM. can we produce a checklist for onboarding and a test payload?
kevin-w: checklist draft: 1) confirm export type (S3 or Webhook). 2) for S3, confirm KMS key ARN and grant audit-exporter-role kms:Decrypt and s3:PutObject rights. 3) provide sample event (current canonical format) + last-stable format they might have seen. 4) provide HMAC signature verification details for webhooks. 5) retention and TTL semantics. 6) compatibility note for lineage fields.
tara: add: instructions for gzip vs jsonl and object naming pattern. customer said their parser expects newline-delimited JSON (JSONL) but our S3 objects were zipped single JSON arrays. we should support both or clearly document which we send per export config.
olivia: agreed. add S3 object pattern and an example: ```/audit/{customer_id}/{year}/{month}/{day}/{service}/{uuid}.json.gz``` and header metadata: Content-Encoding: gzip, Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8, x-redwood-export-format: jsonl|json-array
kevin-w: KMS notes: when using SSE-KMS we encrypt with a service-managed key that rotates. customers using cross-account decryption must: 1) add the KMS key policy to allow their role, or 2) use our cross-account grant flow. we should provide exact policy snippet.
support-sam: they are cross-account. can you paste the minimal policy they need?
kevin-w: sample policy snippet: ```{ "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [{ "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::CUSTOMER_ACC:role/audit-ingest"}, "Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:DescribeKey"], "Resource": "*" }] }``` note: replace PRINCIPAL and tighten Resource to the KMS key ARN.
tara: webhook signing: we sign with HMAC-SHA256 using the shared secret stored in the customer's config. headers: `X-Redwood-Timestamp` and `X-Redwood-Signature`. verification example: ```python
import hmac, hashlib
def verify(body, ts, signature, secret):
    expected = hmac.new(secret.encode(), f"{ts}.{body}".encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature)
```
kevin-w: also document replay window: 5 minutes. reject if |now - ts| > 300s.
olivia: SIEM mapping: provide both flattened fields and the raw event under `raw_event`. encourage customers to map on `event_type` and `actor_id`. if using Splunk HEC, they should set `sourcetype=redwood:audit` and parse JSON, not CSV.
support-sam: for onboarding steps i'll give them: 1) test S3 download: we will send a test file to their bucket (with putObject ACL=private) 2) test KMS decrypt with sample role + policy 3) webhook URL: we will POST 5 test events with valid signatures 4) confirm parsing for both JSONL and JSON-array 5) confirm retention policy & TTL for exports (default 90 days)
ehtan: (probably a typo in participant list) :eyes:
kevin-w: tiny ops note: rollouts — we'll enable the canonical flat schema for all exports next week (canary tomorrow). we need a migration note for customers who relied on nested actor.email. action items: 1) publish schema diff doc, 2) generate sample payloads in both formats, 3) create a support playbook for cross-account KMS grants, 4) patch webhook verification doc.
tara: assigning: kevin -> schema diff + sample payloads, olivia -> support playbook KMS & S3 patterns, support-sam -> outreach + run the test files with acme-telemetry. i'll draft a short customer-facing email template.
support-sam: acked. i'll queue onboarding calls and put the test bucket details in the ticket.
kevin-w: i'll add a compatibility flag that lets exports include `actor_email` for 30 days while we notify customers. planning to push the flag tomorrow morning.
sec-bot: incident-bot: new incident created INC-2026-045: s3-audit-delivery-schema-compat — priority P2. assigned to eng-security.
olivia: thanks. small ask — include a sample Splunk HEC payload in the schema doc, something like: ```{ "time": 1650000000, "host": "redwood-inference", "source": "redwood:audit", "sourcetype": "redwood:audit", "event": {"event_type": "model.deploy", "actor_id": "u-123", "actor_display": "maia"} }```
tara: perfect. i'll follow up with the email template and the link to the schema diff doc once kevin has a draft. :thumbsup:
